summary.headline: Amagi FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,506 crores and turned PAT positive at INR 72 crores, swinging about INR 140 crores from a FY25 loss.
summary.overview: Amagi reported its first full year as a listed company, with FY26 revenue of INR 1,506 crores (up 30% reported, 23% constant currency) and Q4 revenue of INR 397 crores (up 29%). Adjusted EBITDA rose to about INR 156 crores (10% margin) from INR 23 crores, and PAT was INR 72 crores versus a loss of INR 69 crores in FY25. Management stressed net revenue retention of 126% and growth across all three segments, while flagging Q4 gross margin compression tied to customer pricing, AI costs and parallel-running of lower-cost alternatives. NEWSPULSE, the first agentic AI product, has its first paying customer and is in trials with news networks.

segments.name: Streaming unification
segments.commentary: Largest segment at INR 838 crores, up 26% YoY, roughly more than half of revenue; serves OTT, FAST and CTV platforms.

segments.name: Monetization and marketplace
segments.commentary: INR 381 crores, up 36% YoY, about a quarter of revenue and the fastest-growing segment; monetized impressions grew about 62% YoY. Management does not yet report marketplace separately.

segments.name: Cloud modernization
segments.commentary: INR 286 crores, up 32% YoY, about a fifth of revenue; AccuWeather migration to Amagi Cloud completed end-to-end this quarter.

guidance_outlook: No prescriptive FY27 guidance; management aspires to keep growing at a healthy clip, citing the trajectory of the last three years.
Focus areas for FY27 are durable revenue growth, operating leverage and cash conversion.
Current margin levels are not steady state; management sees headroom and upside, and will make ahead-of-curve AI investments.

Gross margin: management said not to extrapolate quarterly moves to full year and expects volume growth to offset modest CPM/price compression; the gross margin impact of NEWSPULSE is too early to quantify.
Seasonality: Q1 is about 22% of full-year revenue and about 11% of adjusted EBITDA; H1 is about 45% of revenue and H2 about 55%, with EBITDA about 37% in H1 and 63% in H2.
Management said no hedging book is in place; it is considering hedging this year given the net USD revenue position.
capex_capacity: Cost-side plan: R&D is being redirected toward next-generation agentic products; R&D fell from 33% to 23% of revenue over FY24-FY26.
Cloud modernization is in early innings; serviceable addressable revenue grew about 11% to USD 1.9 billion this year.
Management is scanning for buy-or-build acquisitions in glass-to-glass gaps, with no deal size fixed and no specific target named.
demand_pricing: Dollar-based NRR is north of 120%, in a 120% to 125% range for several years; management says it is comfortable even after currency adjustment.
Monetized impression growth of about 62% YoY came with revenue growth of 36%, implying modest CPM pressure offset by volume.
Q4 gross margin fell sequentially on customer pricing (renegotiation), AI costs (minor) and double-running costs of lower-cost alternatives on mission-critical workflows.
NEWSPULSE targets traditional news networks; tens of POCs are running, and management said it is too early to share sales-cycle or unit-economics detail.
No competitor seen as credible at platform level; management says customers prefer one unified platform over many point solutions.
Partnerships: ADAMS (Latin America), Anoki (ad partner), Vodafone deal in Germany, with progress in Australia and the US.

qa_highlights.question: Split of NEWSPULSE paid customers between cross-sell to existing Amagi clients and new logos, and unit economics or gross margin of the agentic product.
qa_highlights.answer: Existing customers are the first port of call, but NEWSPULSE is also landing new logos; tens of POCs are running and detail will come in coming quarters. Gross margin impact is too early to quantify; outcome-based pricing mixed with fixed fees, and no major margin impact seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin compression QoQ: how much was client renegotiation versus AI and investment costs, and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: customer pricing, AI cost (minor), and double-running costs of lower-cost alternatives. Management says full-year gross margin has held at about 69% and sees volume growth offsetting modest price compression.

qa_highlights.question: Sales headcount efficiency and how many accounts one salesperson can handle over 3 to 5 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Account management is sublinear in scale given NRR of 126%; product-led growth and AI tooling should lift efficiency. No revenue-share model; commissions are sliding-scale by hunter or farmer role.

qa_highlights.question: Does accelerating monetized impression growth reflect market conditions, and how exposed is revenue to advertising macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Impression growth reflects the shift to streaming. Customers' ad economics flow through to Amagi pricing with a lag; no impact seen yet, though geopolitics is a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count trend and new customer additions, which have slowed on a quarterly basis.
qa_highlights.answer: Customer count rose to 492 in FY26 from 463 and 396 earlier; Q4 added 27 and churned 30, mainly year-end cleanup of sub-USD 1,000 accounts. Growth is coming from the existing base and upmarket enterprise deals.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and acquisition plans, and CC NRR.
qa_highlights.answer: Corp Dev is scanning buy-or-build options in glass-to-glass gaps, with no size set and no irrational valuations. Dollar-based NRR is above 120%.

qa_highlights.question: Path to higher PAT margin and whether 5% is steady state.
qa_highlights.answer: Management says current margins are not steady state and that there is headroom, but will keep making ahead-of-curve AI investments.

risks_watch: Gross margin: Q4 compression from customer pricing and dual-running costs; the June quarter trend and whether pricing pressure outruns volume gains.
AI monetisation: NEWSPULSE has one paying customer so far; gross margin and unit economics remain unproven.
Customer churn and count: 30 accounts churned in Q4, and the net count rose only modestly.
Currency: most revenue is USD; about 30% of costs are direct costs and about 20% are USD-linked sales costs, with no formal hedge book.
Advertising macro: revenue is linked to customer ad spend, and management flagged geopolitical risk.
Acquisitions: cash of about INR 1,664 crores with no size or target set; deal and integration risk if pursued.
summary.management_tone: Confident and balanced on FY26 delivery and retention metrics, with explicit caution that Q4 gross margin and NEWSPULSE economics are early. Management was evasive on FY27 numeric guidance, offering only qualitative aspirations.
